policy_title: Expand Royal Navy Overseas Patrol Squadron and assess dedicated coast guard
stated: Reform UK will expand the Royal Navy Overseas Patrol Squadron to police Britain's 200 nautical mile EEZ properly, and assess the possibility of creating a dedicated coast guard or fisheries protection agency.

source.quote: Expand the Royal Navy Overseas Patrol Squadron Police Britain’s 200 nautical mile EEZ properly. Assess the possibility of creating a dedicated coast guard or fisheries protection agency.

bearing_set.reason: Expanding naval patrol capacity and assessing a coast guard directly bears on national security, maritime border security, and enforcement capability — all core O5 indicators.

Enlarging the Royal Navy Overseas Patrol Squadron and potentially standing up a new coast guard or fisheries agency represents a concrete increase in public expenditure; the fiscal cost mechanism is clear and non-negligible.

membership_note: The policy bears primarily on maritime security (O5) and the public spending required to deliver it (O12). The fisheries-industry economic upside is real but too small in aggregate (UK fishing ~0.04% of GDP) to clear the non-negligible bar for O13; the assessment phase for the coast guard makes any O10 surveillance concern too speculative to score.
